title: Principal Capability Separation
intent: Separate actor identity from narrowly scoped execution authority.
problem: Without principal resolution followed by capability scope verification, the system can accept an outcome that is not justified by the principal capability separation contract.
context: This pattern addresses actors receive task-scoped authority; its concrete control is principal resolution followed by capability scope verification.
forces: Correctness requires that identity alone grants no operation
Operational pressure can cause: role claims are mistaken for capabilities
solution: Implement principal resolution followed by capability scope verification. Verify the anchored symbol `utcnow` with `test_health` before reuse.
invariants: capability subject must equal the resolved principal
failure_modes: role claims are mistaken for capabilities
a capability is accepted for another subject
security: The security boundary specifically rejects `role claims are mistaken for capabilities` and fails closed if the principal capability separation evidence cannot be verified.
privacy: For principal capability separation, persist only its decision identifiers and digests; exclude payload data unrelated to principal resolution followed by capability scope verification.
reuse_constraints: Confirm the target still requires: actors receive task-scoped authority
Do not apply when: a trusted single-user offline utility has no authorization boundary
External Ethernian promotion signature remains mandatory
not_when: a trusted single-user offline utility has no authorization boundary
